messages:
Alex: FYI nightly perf job fired a regression alert for small-batch latency (median +18%). CI link: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/runs/1769123 :warning:

Maria: saw that. summary from CI bot? did it point to a particular model or hardware?

ci-bot: Nightly perf job: run=1769123, suite=small-batch-throughput, model=gpt-small-q4, host=gpu-01, median_latency_ms=12.4 (baseline 10.5), p95=35.2 -> +25%

Kevin: interesting, gpt-small-q4 had a quantization kernel tweak in #4921 yesterday. cc @Alex @Maria

Alex: yep merged the kernel fallback for some aten ops. I didn't expect perf regression but possible for short sequences.

Sam: Can we reproduce locally quickly? suggested repro command: `./tools/bench --model gpt-small-q4 --batch 2 --seq 64 --profile perf.json`

Maria: trying that now on my dev box (nv4) — will report perf.json.

Jen: if it's kernel-related we should also try a run pinned to the pre-#4921 commit to confirm. e.g. `git checkout a1b2c3 && bazel build //runtime:inference && ./tools/bench ...`

Kevin: good call. I'll kick off a bisect script across the last 10 merges to isolate.

Alex: for triage let's collect: perf trace, `nvidia-smi` output, kernel selection logs (`LOG_KERNEL=1`), and a short flamegraph from `--profiler=lite`. Put artifacts in /tmp/perf-1769123 and attach here.

Maria: attached perf.json and flamegraph.svg to the run. quick diff: median 10.6 @ a1b2c3 vs 12.5 @ HEAD. p95 variance larger.

Kevin: ran bisect-ish: culprit looks like commit 8f9d7 (the aten fallback). rolling back that change locally drops median back ~10.4. patch likely changes kernel path for sequence len < 128.

Sam: if that's the case maybe the fallback is choosing a safer but slower kernel. Is there a metric that indicates which kernel was selected?

Alex: yes, enable `RUNTIME_KERNEL_TRACE=1` for bench. it will print chosen kernel names and timings.

Maria: re-ran with trace, snippet: ```
kernel=matmul_opt_v2, seq=64, time=0.78ms
kernel=matmul_fallback, seq=64, time=1.02ms
```
looks like fallback being used on the critical path.

Jen: does matmul_opt_v2 have a correctness issue for some edge shapes? fallback added because of instability in older drivers. Could be we regressed the cost model that biases toward fallback.

Kevin: hypothesis: fallback heuristics now trigger for quantized kernels due to a rounding of the heuristics threshold. I'll prepare a small PR to adjust the threshold and add a unit perf test.

Alex: thanks. short mitigation: we can pin the scheduled nightly to the previous runtime build until we ship fix. Ops team, flag? @Sam can you escalate to releases?

Sam: on it — creating a rollback schedule for the nightly-only pipeline, not production. will comment with timestamp.

Maria: also noted this affects only small-batch (<4) workloads. larger batches have expected gains. worth documenting in the release notes.

Kevin: PR incoming in a few hours: #4960 — adjusts decision threshold + adds kernel selection debug metric to metrics/host. adding an e2e perf check in CI too.

Alex: sounds good. owners for next steps: Kevin (fix + PR), Maria (verify perf on nv4/nv8), Sam (rollback nightly), Jen (validate correctness for edge cases). I'll follow up with a short postmortem once fixed.

Jen: sgtm. quick ask — Kevin can you include a reproducible bench config in the PR so QE can run?

Kevin: will do. also adding `--samples 50` to stabilize numbers.

ci-bot: Note: I scheduled a re-run of the nightly job with current HEAD in 20m.

Maria: running a smoke with the new trace flags now, will paste results when done.

Alex: thanks everyone. low churn thread, will update when PR merges. :thumbsup:
